projectCategory: DSA Module 6.2: Segment Trees Architecture & Lazy Propagation Mechanics
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Segment Tree Array Construction for Range Sum Queries
projects.description: A Segment Tree is a full binary tree data structure represented as an array of size `4 * N` that enables range queries (sum, min, max, gcd) over an array of size N in logarithmic O(log N) time! Build the tree recursively: node `node` at range `[start, end]` computes `tree[node] = tree[2*node] + tree[2*node+1]` in O(N) time. In this project, you will build a Segment Tree Range Sum Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Segment Tree Tree Array Representation, Recursive Divide & Conquer Build & Range Sum Queries
projects.exampleText: Build tree for [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11] and query sum [1..3]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Segment Tree Range Sum Query ---
Range Sum [1..3] (3+5+7) = 15
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Recursive Build**: Subdivide `[start, end]` into `[start, mid]` and `[mid+1, end]`.
2. **Query Overlap**: 3 cases for range query: Complete Outside (return 0), Complete Inside (return `tree[node]`), Partial Overlap (combine left + right children).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `build_tree()` & `query_sum()`: Constructs Segment Tree array and answers range sum queries in O(log N).

projects.title: Point Update and Range Sum Query in Segment Tree
projects.description: Modify an array element `arr[idx] = val` and update all affected Segment Tree internal nodes along the path from leaf to root in logarithmic O(log N) time! Recurse down to leaf `start == end == idx`, update value, and combine child values during recursion return. In this project, you will build Point Update Segment Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Point Update Traversal, Path Node Value Recalculation & Logarithmic Time Guarantee
projects.exampleText: Update arr[2] = 10 in O(log N) time
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Point Update in Segment Tree ---
Updated element at index 2 to value 10 in O(log N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Leaf Traversal**: Traverse down to leaf node where `start == end == idx`.
2. **Return Re-computation**: Recompute `tree[node] = tree[2*node] + tree[2*node+1]` while unwinding stack.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `update_point()`: Updates single array element in Segment Tree in O(log N) time.

projects.title: Range Minimum Query (RMQ) Segment Tree
projects.description: Answer Range Minimum Queries `min(arr[L .. R])` in O(log N) time. Internal tree nodes store `tree[node] = min(tree[2*node], tree[2*node+1])`. Outside range queries return `INT_MAX`. In this project, you will build Range Minimum Query (RMQ) Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Range Minimum Queries (RMQ), Neutral Value Return (`INT_MAX`) & Min Combination Logic
projects.exampleText: Find minimum in range [1..4]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Minimum Query (RMQ) Segment Tree ---
Range Minimum Query RMQ[1..4] = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min Combination**: Node stores `min(left_child, right_child)`.
2. **Outside Boundary**: Return `INT_MAX` for out-of-bounds queries.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `rmq_demo()`: Solves Range Minimum Queries using Segment Tree.

projects.title: Range Maximum Query Segment Tree with Point Update
projects.description: Answer Range Maximum Queries `max(arr[L .. R])` and support dynamic point updates `arr[idx] = val` in O(log N) time. Outside range queries return `INT_MIN`. In this project, you will build Range Maximum Query Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Range Maximum Queries, Neutral Value Return (`INT_MIN`) & Point Update Propagation
projects.exampleText: Find maximum in range [2..5]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Maximum Query Segment Tree ---
Range Maximum Query [2..5] = 99
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Max Combination**: Node stores `max(left_child, right_child)`.
2. **Outside Boundary**: Return `INT_MIN` for out-of-bounds queries.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `range_max_demo()`: Computes Range Maximum Queries using Segment Tree.

projects.title: Range GCD Query Segment Tree
projects.description: Answer Range Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) queries `gcd(arr[L .. R])` in O(log N * log(MAX_VAL)) time. Internal nodes store `tree[node] = gcd(tree[2*node], tree[2*node+1])`. Neutral return value is `0` (`gcd(x, 0) = x`). In this project, you will build Range GCD Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Euclidean GCD Merge Logic, Neutral Return Value (0) & Range Number Theory Queries
projects.exampleText: Find range GCD for [12, 18, 24, 36] in range [0..3]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range GCD Query Segment Tree ---
Range GCD Query [0..3] for [12, 18, 24, 36] = 6
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **GCD Merge**: Node stores `gcd(left_child, right_child)`.
2. **Neutral Identity**: Return `0` for out-of-bounds segments.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `range_gcd_demo()`: Solves Range GCD Queries using Segment Tree.

projects.title: Lazy Propagation Fundamental Mechanics (updateRange in O(log N))
projects.description: Applying range updates `arr[L..R] += val` to N leaf nodes individually takes O(N log N) time. **Lazy Propagation** delays updates to child nodes until necessary by storing pending updates in a `lazy[node]` array. Reduces range update time complexity to logarithmic O(log N)! In this project, you will build Lazy Propagation Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Lazy Propagation Architecture, Pending Update Storage `lazy[]` & Push Function Mechanics
projects.exampleText: Apply range addition update +5 to range [2..6]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Lazy Propagation Fundamental Mechanics ---
Applied +5 to range [2..6] in O(log N) time using Lazy Propagation.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Push Pending**: Before processing node, push pending `lazy[node]` values to children.
2. **Lazy Tagging**: If current segment `[start, end]` is completely inside update range `[L, R]`, mark `lazy[node] += val` and push immediately.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `update_range_lazy()` & `push()`: Executes range updates using Lazy Propagation in O(log N) time.

projects.title: Range Addition Updates with Lazy Propagation
projects.description: Support both Range Addition updates `arr[L..R] += V` and Range Sum queries `sum(arr[L..R])` in O(log N) time. When pushing lazy additions: `tree[node] += (end - start + 1) * lazy[node]`. In this project, you will build Range Addition Lazy Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Range Addition Lazy Formulas, Segment Length Multiplications & O(log N) Queries
projects.exampleText: Update range [1..3] += 10 and query range sum
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Addition Updates with Lazy Propagation ---
Range sum query after +10 update to [1..3] = 45
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Additive Lazy Update**: `tree[node] += len * lazy[node]`.
2. **Child Propagation**: Add `lazy[node]` to `lazy[left]` and `lazy[right]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `range_addition_lazy_demo()`: Executes Range Addition updates with Lazy Propagation.

projects.title: Range Assignment / Set Updates with Lazy Propagation
projects.description: Support Range Assignment updates `arr[L..R] = V` (overwriting range elements with constant value V). When pushing lazy assignments: `tree[node] = (end - start + 1) * lazy[node]`. Lazy values override previous un-propagated assignments! In this project, you will build Range Assignment Lazy Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Range Assignment Updates, Overwriting Lazy Tags & Range Value Overrides
projects.exampleText: Assign range [2..5] = 7 using Lazy Propagation
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Assignment / Set Updates with Lazy Propagation ---
Set range [2..5] to value 7 in O(log N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Assignment Update**: `tree[node] = len * lazy[node]`.
2. **Lazy Override**: Overwrite `lazy[left] = lazy[right] = lazy[node]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `range_assignment_lazy_demo()`: Executes Range Assignment updates with Lazy Propagation.

projects.title: Count Even / Odd Numbers in Range Query Segment Tree
projects.description: Answer queries returning the number of even numbers (or odd numbers) in range `[L..R]`. Each tree node stores struct `{ int evens; int odds; }`. Point updates flip or update counts in O(log N) time! In this project, you will build Even/Odd Counter Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Composite Struct Tree Nodes, Parity Counter Merges & Range Frequency Queries
projects.exampleText: Count even numbers in range [1..5]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Even / Odd Numbers in Range Query ---
Even numbers count in range [1..5] = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Struct Merge**: `node.evens = left.evens + right.evens`.
2. **Parity Query**: Combine even counters across query segment overlap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `even_odd_segment_tree_demo()`: Counts even/odd numbers in range queries.

projects.title: Iterative Non-Recursive Segment Tree Implementation
projects.description: Standard recursive Segment Trees use function call stack overhead. An Iterative (Non-Recursive) Segment Tree stores leaves at indices `N .. 2N - 1` and uses bitwise shifts `i >> 1` and bitwise OR `i ^ 1` to execute point updates and range queries in 4x less memory and faster execution time! In this project, you will build Iterative Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Iterative Segment Trees, Bitwise Pointer Shifts (`p >> 1`, `p ^ 1`) & Non-Recursive Performance
projects.exampleText: Execute range query [1..3] on iterative Segment Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Iterative Non-Recursive Segment Tree ---
Range Sum [1..3] = 9
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Leaf Indexing**: Array elements placed at `tree[N + i]`.
2. **Bitwise Query Loop**: Shift `l += N, r += N + 1` up tree using `l >>= 1, r >>= 1`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `build_iterative()`, `update_iterative()`, `query_iterative()`: Implements iterative non-recursive Segment Tree.

projects.title: Segment Tree for Maximum Subarray Sum in Range (Kadane's Query Engine)
projects.description: Answer queries for Maximum Contiguous Subarray Sum (Kadane's algorithm) over ANY range `[L..R]` in O(log N) time! Each tree node maintains a struct: `{ total_sum, max_prefix, max_suffix, max_subarray_sum }`. In this project, you will build Maximum Subarray Sum Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Kadane Range Queries, Node Struct Merges & Prefix/Suffix Subarray Mechanics
projects.exampleText: Query maximum subarray sum in range [1..4]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Subarray Sum in Range (Kadane Segment Tree) ---
Maximum Subarray Sum in Query Range [1..4] = 18
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Node Struct**: Store `sum, pref, suff, max_sub`.
2. **Merge Formula**: `node.max_sub = max(left.max_sub, right.max_sub, left.suff + right.pref)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_subarray_sum_segment_tree_demo()`: Solves Range Maximum Subarray Sum via Segment Tree.

projects.title: Range Flip Bits Queries (Lazy Propagation Binary Inversion)
projects.description: Given a binary array of 0s and 1s, support Range Flip updates `arr[L..R] ^= 1` and Range 1-bit Count queries. Pushing lazy flip flag `lazy[node] ^= 1` swaps node's 1-bits and 0-bits: `ones = (end - start + 1) - ones` in O(log N) time! In this project, you will build Range Flip Bits Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Binary Inversion Lazy Propagation, XOR Tag Flipping & Range Bit Flipping
projects.exampleText: Flip bits in range [2..6] and query 1-bit count
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Flip Bits Queries (Lazy Propagation) ---
Count of 1-bits in range [2..6] after bit flip update = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Flip Formula**: `ones = segment_len - ones`.
2. **Lazy Inversion**: `lazy[node] ^= 1` toggles flip status.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `range_flip_bits_demo()`: Executes Range Bit Flip updates with Lazy Propagation.

projects.title: Persistent Segment Tree (Versioned Array State Snapshots)
projects.description: A Persistent Segment Tree preserves ALL previous versions of an array after point updates. Instead of modifying nodes in-place, copy updated nodes and allocate new tree roots (`root[v]`). Each update allocates only `O(log N)` new nodes while sharing un-modified subtrees! In this project, you will build Persistent Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Persistent Data Structures, Versioned Tree Roots & Subtree Node Sharing
projects.exampleText: Query range sum across multiple array versions
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Persistent Segment Tree (Versioned State Snapshots) ---
Query Sum at Version 1 [0..3] = 10
Query Sum at Version 2 [0..3] = 25
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Node Copy**: Copy updated path nodes; point unchanged child pointers to existing version nodes.
2. **Version Roots**: Store root pointer `root[version]` for every update version.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `persistent_segment_tree_demo()`: Implements Persistent Segment Tree version snapshots.

projects.title: Dynamic Segment Tree with Pointer Allocation
projects.description: When coordinate ranges are huge (e.g. `0 <= N <= 10^9`), allocating a static array of size `4 * 10^9` is impossible. A Dynamic Segment Tree allocates child nodes dynamically using pointers ONLY when visited, consuming `O(Q log N)` memory! In this project, you will build Dynamic Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Pointer Allocation, Sparse Coordinate Ranges & Sparse Tree Node Creation
projects.exampleText: Query range [0..10^9] on dynamic sparse Segment Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic Segment Tree (Pointer Allocation) ---
Allocated sparse nodes dynamically for range [0..10^9]. Range Sum = 42
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **On-Demand Allocation**: Create `node->left` or `node->right` dynamically when child visited.
2. **Coordinate Compression Avoidance**: Handles huge 10^9 range queries directly.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dynamic_segment_tree_demo()`: Solves sparse large-range queries via Dynamic Segment Tree.

projects.title: 2D Segment Tree for Matrix Subgrid Range Queries
projects.description: A 2D Segment Tree is a Segment Tree where each node is ITSELF a Segment Tree! Supports 2D submatrix range queries `[(r1,c1)..(r2,c2)]` and point updates `matrix[r][c] = val` in `O(log R * log C)` time! In this project, you will build 2D Subgrid Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Segment Tree Architecture, Nested Outer/Inner Segment Trees & Submatrix Queries
projects.exampleText: Query 2D submatrix sum [(1,1)..(3,3)]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 2D Segment Tree for Matrix Subgrid Queries ---
Submatrix 2D Range Sum [(1,1)..(3,3)] = 120
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Nested Trees**: Outer tree manages matrix rows; inner trees manage matrix columns.
2. **2D Query**: Combine 2D subgrid range queries in `O(log R * log C)` time.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `segment_tree_2d_demo()`: Solves 2D matrix range queries using 2D Segment Tree.

projects.title: Count Inversions in Array using Segment Tree
projects.description: An inversion is a pair `(i, j)` where `i < j` and `arr[i] > arr[j]`. Insert elements into a frequency Segment Tree one by one: query range sum `[arr[i]+1 .. MAX_VAL]` to count numbers greater than `arr[i]` seen so far in O(N log N) time! In this project, you will build Segment Tree Inversion Counter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Frequency Segment Trees, Range Count Queries & Inversion Pair Counting
projects.exampleText: Count inversions in array using Segment Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Inversions in Array via Segment Tree ---
Total Inversions Count = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Tree**: Leaf `v` stores frequency of value `v`.
2. **Query & Update**: For each element, query sum `[arr[i]+1 .. MAX]`, then increment `tree[arr[i]]++`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `count_inversions_segment_tree_demo()`: Counts array inversions using Segment Tree.

projects.title: K-th Smallest Element in Range Query (Persistent Segment Tree)
projects.description: Find the K-th smallest element in subarray range `[L .. R]` in O(log N) time! Build a Persistent Segment Tree of element frequency prefixes `root[0..N]`. Binary search on tree version diff `root[R] - root[L-1]` to locate K-th element in O(log N) time! In this project, you will build K-th Smallest Range Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Persistent Frequency Trees, Range Version Differences & Binary Search on Trees
projects.exampleText: Find 3rd smallest element in range [1..4]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- K-th Smallest Element in Range Query (Persistent) ---
3rd Smallest Element in Range [1..4] = 7
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Version Diff**: `count = root[R].left_count - root[L-1].left_count`.
2. **Tree Walk**: If `K <= count`, recurse left; else `K -= count`, recurse right.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `kth_smallest_persistent_demo()`: Finds K-th smallest element in range using Persistent Segment Tree.

projects.title: Range Sum Queries with Range Multiply and Range Add Lazy Updates
projects.description: Support both Range Multiplication `arr[L..R] *= M` AND Range Addition `arr[L..R] += A` using Lazy Propagation. Combine lazy tags: `lazy_add = (lazy_add * M + A) % MOD` and `lazy_mul = (lazy_mul * M) % MOD`. In this project, you will build Multiply & Add Lazy Segment Tree in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Combined Lazy Tags, Composition of Affine Transformations & Modulo Maintenance
projects.exampleText: Execute range multiply (*2) and range add (+3) lazy updates
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Range Multiply and Range Add Lazy Updates ---
Range Sum after range multiply (*2) and range add (+3) = 98
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Affine Tag Combination**: New value `x * mul + add`.
2. **Composition Rules**: Update `mul` tag and adjust `add` tag proportionally.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `multiply_add_lazy_demo()`: Solves range multiply and range add lazy updates.

projects.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) using Segment Tree
projects.description: Find Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) in O(N log N) time using a Maximum Segment Tree over coordinate-compressed values. For element `X`, query max LIS length in range `[0 .. X-1]`, then update `tree[X] = max_lis + 1`. In this project, you will build LIS Segment Tree Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: DP Acceleration via Segment Trees, Coordinate Compression & Range Max Queries
projects.exampleText: Compute LIS length via Segment Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) via Segment Tree ---
Longest Increasing Subsequence Length = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Coordinate Compression**: Map elements to `0..N-1` range.
2. **Tree DP Update**: `tree[X] = query_max(0, X - 1) + 1`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lis_segment_tree_demo()`: Solves LIS in O(N log N) using Segment Tree.

projects.title: Segment Tree Walk (Binary Search on Segment Tree in O(log N))
projects.description: Find the FIRST index in array where prefix sum is `>= target` WITHOUT performing standard binary search `O(log^2 N)`. Walk down the Segment Tree directly: compare target with left child sum `tree[2*node]` to decide left vs right child branch in optimal `O(log N)` time! In this project, you will build Segment Tree Walk Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Segment Tree Walk, Binary Search Tree Elimination & Logarithmic Target Locating
projects.exampleText: Find first index with prefix sum >= 15
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Segment Tree Walk (Binary Search on Segment Tree) ---
First index with prefix sum >= 15 is Index 3 (Found in O(log N) time).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Direct Walk**: If `tree[left] >= target`, recurse left; else `target -= tree[left]`, recurse right.
2. **O(log N) Time**: Replaces nested O(log^2 N) binary search with single tree descent.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `segment_tree_walk_demo()`: Solves binary search on Segment Tree in O(log N) time.

projects.title: Segment Tree Beats (Beats Algorithm / Chmin & Chmax Range Operations)
projects.description: The Segment Tree Beats (Ji Ruyi Algorithm) supports non-linear range operations like `arr[i] = min(arr[i], V)` (Range Chmin) and `arr[i] = max(arr[i], V)` (Range Chmax) in O(log N) amortized time by tracking max, 2nd max, and max count in tree nodes! In this project, you will build Segment Tree Beats Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Segment Tree Beats Algorithm, 2nd Maximum Tracking & Amortized Non-Linear Updates
projects.exampleText: Execute Range Chmin update `arr[i] = min(arr[i], V)`
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Segment Tree Beats (Chmin & Chmax Range Operations) ---
Executed range chmin update `arr[i] = min(arr[i], V)` in O(log N) amortized time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Track 2nd Max**: Node stores `max1`, `max2`, and `count_max1`.
2. **Beats Pruning**: If `V >= max1`, break; if `max2 < V < max1`, apply update to `max1` and tag lazy; else recurse.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `segment_tree_beats_demo()`: Solves Segment Tree Beats non-linear range operations.

projects.title: Heavy-Light Decomposition (HLD) + Segment Tree for Tree Path Queries
projects.description: Heavy-Light Decomposition (HLD) partitions a general tree of N nodes into `O(log N)` contiguous linear chains mapped into a single Segment Tree. Enables tree path queries `queryPath(u, v)` and path updates in `O(log^2 N)` time! In this project, you will build HLD Segment Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Heavy-Light Decomposition (HLD), Heavy/Light Edge Partitioning & Tree Path Segment Queries
projects.exampleText: Execute path query `queryPath(u, v)` on tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Heavy-Light Decomposition (HLD) + Segment Tree ---
Executed tree path query `queryPath(u, v)` in O(log^2 N) time via HLD Segment Tree.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **HLD Partition**: Decompose tree into heavy chains based on child subtree size.
2. **Segment Mapping**: Flatten heavy chains into continuous Segment Tree index ranges.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hld_segment_tree_demo()`: Solves tree path queries using HLD + Segment Tree.

projects.title: Segment Tree Merging (Tree Dynamic Node Merging)
projects.description: Segment Tree Merging merges two Dynamic Segment Trees of sizes `S1` and `S2` in `O(min(S1, S2))` time. Used in tree algorithms to combine subtree frequency segment trees from children to parent in `O(N log N)` overall time! In this project, you will build Segment Tree Merging Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Segment Tree Merging, Subtree Frequency Tree Combination & Dynamic Node Merging
projects.exampleText: Merge child dynamic segment trees into parent node
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Segment Tree Merging (Dynamic Node Merging) ---
Merged child subtree dynamic segment trees into parent node in O(N log N) total time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Node Merge**: If node missing in tree 1, return node of tree 2. Combine node values if both present.
2. **Recurse Merging**: Recurse down left and right children recursively.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `segment_tree_merging_demo()`: Implements Segment Tree Merging algorithm.

projects.title: Parallel SIMD-Accelerated Vector Segment Tree Kernel
projects.description: High-speed graphics and financial trading systems accelerate Segment Tree updates using SIMD 256-bit AVX2 vector instructions, updating 8 child tree nodes simultaneously in 1 CPU clock cycle! In this project, you will build SIMD Segment Tree Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SIMD AVX2 Vector Tree Processing, Hardware-Parallel Node Updates & High-Frequency Trading
projects.exampleText: Evaluate 8 child node updates in 256-bit AVX2 vector register
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel SIMD-Accelerated Vector Segment Tree Kernel ---
Evaluated 8 segment tree child node updates concurrently in 256-bit AVX2 registers.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Vector Register**: Load 8 child node values into 256-bit AVX2 register.
2. **Hardware Parallel Sum**: Compute 8 SIMD vector segment tree updates in single clock pass.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `simd_segment_tree_demo()`: Simulates SIMD vector accelerated Segment Tree kernel.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Stream Segment Tree
projects.description: Process 1,000,000 streaming telemetry range queries per second by embedding Segment Trees directly inside memory-mapped shared memory buffers (`mmap`). In this project, you will build Real-Time Stream Segment Tree Simulator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped Segment Tree Buffers, High-Throughput Stream Range Queries & Telemetry Engine

projects.exampleOutput:
--- High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Stream Segment Tree ---
Processed 1,000,000 streaming telemetry range queries per second.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Memory-Mapped Buffer**: Allocate Segment Tree in shared memory buffer.
2. **Stream Update**: Update telemetry range values in real-time with zero system-call overhead.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stream_segment_tree_demo()`: Simulates high-throughput real-time stream Segment Tree kernel.
